## 1. The smooth rock with soil on it  (`#the-rock-with-soil`)

Cited ayat: 2:264

> **2:264** يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تُبْطِلُوا۟ صَدَقَٰتِكُم بِٱلْمَنِّ وَٱلْأَذَىٰ كَٱلَّذِى يُنفِقُ مَالَهُۥ رِئَآءَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَا يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْـَٔاخِرِ فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ صَفْوَانٍ عَلَيْهِ تُرَابٌ فَأَصَابَهُۥ وَابِلٌ فَتَرَكَهُۥ صَلْدًا لَّا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍ مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا۟ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (2:264): The ayah tells those who believe not to cancel their charity with reminders of favours and with hurt, like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people and does not believe in God and the last day.

**c2** (2:264): His similitude is that of a smooth rock with soil on it; a heavy rain hits it and leaves it bare, and they have no power over anything they have earned.

**c3** (2:264): The ayah ends by saying that God does not guide the disbelieving people.

### One-minute summary

The ayah tells those who believe not to cancel their charity with reminders of favours and with hurt [c1]. It likens the one who spends to be seen by people to a smooth rock with soil on it that a heavy rain leaves bare [c1][c2].

### Complete story

The ayah tells those who believe not to cancel their charity with reminders of favours and with hurt [c1]. This is like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people and does not believe in God and the last day [c1].

His similitude is that of a smooth rock with soil on it [c2]. A heavy rain hits it and leaves it bare, and they have no power over anything they have earned [c2]. The ayah ends by saying that God does not guide the disbelieving people [c3].

### Deep study

The ayah gives the comparison in steps: the believers are told what not to do, the one who spends to be seen is described, and then his similitude is given [c1][c2]. The rock and the soil are the picture, and the heavy rain is what leaves the rock bare [c2].

### Kids mode

God tells those who believe not to spoil their charity by reminding people of favours or by hurting them [c1]. A smooth rock with soil on it is left bare by a heavy rain [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah links the cancelling of charity with reminders of favours, with hurt and with spending to be seen by people [c1]. Another reading is that the picture shows what seems to be there, the soil, being washed from bare rock [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who is meant by the one who spends to be seen by people beyond the description in the ayah; no person is named.
- Not established: what the soil stands for beyond the picture the ayah gives.
- The ayah itself uses the word for a similitude (mathal) of this person.
- The Arabic words al-mann and al-adha are rendered 'reminders of favours' and 'hurt'; a scholar should check this wording.
